item.title: She Was Living In The Same City All Along
item.description: Melissa Highsmith was abducted from Fort Worth as a 21-month-old in 1971. More than five decades later, a 23andMe DNA match led her biological family to her, and official testing confirmed her identity in 2023. She had been living under another name in the same city.

item.title: He Walked Away In 2019 And Was Found Six Years Later
item.description: Chance Englebert disappeared after walking away from his wife’s grandparents’ home in Nebraska in July 2019. After years of searches and unanswered questions, his remains were discovered at Scotts Bluff National Monument in 2025, and authorities ruled his death accidental.

item.title: A Pastor Returned Home To A Crime Scene
item.description: Amanda Blackburn was killed during a 2015 home invasion in Indianapolis while her husband was away at the gym. Investigators arrested three men in connection with the case; Larry Jo Taylor Jr. was later convicted of her murder, while two others pleaded guilty to related charges.

item.title: An Affair Ended With A Deadly Parking Lot Confrontation
item.description: In 2011, Idaho attorney Emmett Corrigan was shot and killed after an affair with Kandi Hall, whose husband Robert had confronted the pair. Hall claimed self-defense, but a jury convicted him of second-degree murder and he was sentenced to 30 years in prison.

item.title: She Was Killed In Her Driveway With Cameras Rolling
item.description: Elizabeth Barraza was setting up a garage sale outside her Texas home in January 2019 when an unknown person approached and shot her. Surveillance cameras captured the attack and the suspect’s truck, but despite a $50,000 reward, her murder remains unsolved.

item.title: He Fooled Police Until One Detail Changed Everything
item.description: In 1995, Mark Winger told police he had shot an intruder while defending his wife, Donnah. The case was initially treated as self-defense, but years later a witness and overlooked crime-scene photographs helped expose a different story, leading to Winger’s 2002 conviction for both murders.

item.title: She Didn’t Know Her Husband Had Cut Her Out
item.description: Before his death in 2022, Eric Richins quietly changed his estate plan, removing his wife Kouri and placing his assets in a trust for their children. Prosecutors later alleged she killed him for financial gain; in 2026, a jury convicted her of aggravated murder.

item.title: The Family From Wife Swap Ended In Tragedy
item.description: The Stockdale family appeared on Wife Swap in 2008, gaining attention for their strict, sheltered lifestyle. Nine years later, Jacob Stockdale killed his mother and brother before attempting suicide. He survived, later pleaded guilty to both murders and was sentenced to 30 years to life.

item.title: The Coffee Lawsuit That Wasn't What People Thought
item.description: In 1992, 79-year-old Stella Liebeck suffered severe burns after spilling McDonald’s coffee in a parked car. She initially sought $20,000 for her medical costs, but the case went to trial after McDonald’s offered $800, leading to a widely misunderstood jury verdict.
